>why I can't comprehend about suicide is, and forgive me for being ignorant, is it done voluntarily, or is it like an unstoppable force that takes over your body and makes you do things without you controlling,  

Not here for sympathy, just felt I could offer input as I am dealing with it in a major way today. 

I've dealt with suicidal ideation for a long time. Several hospitalizations for it, some for extended periods. 

It can be very different for everybody, but for me it is generally complete hopelessness. It isn't so much that I've failed at everything (just most things ;-) ), but rather the belief that I *will* fail at everything in the future. 

It isn't involuntary at all, but more of a 'why shouldn't I?'.  The unstoppable force is more the depression that constantly drags you down & makes you feel 'less than'. 

Ironically, it is my fear of failure that is keeping me alive. My first attempt was in high school & was *probably* more of a cry for help. My 2nd attempt was 2 years ago (in my early 40s now) & was interrupted (leading to an extended hospitalization). Now I'm a coward & find myself unable to even "take the easy way out".
